v.why: Replacing a 3x3 conv on edge 1->3 with pooling consistently lost accuracy (exps 41,42,43,48), unlike replacing weaker ops.
Dropping a parameter-free skip on edge 1->3 helped strongly (exps 84,89) while dropping a conv there usually hurt.
With an input->output skip present, removing edge 1->3 hurt on all datasets (exps 81,83,88), leaving the output dominated by the identity path.
Adding a residual input->output path where none existed gave large gains (exps 15,17), more than replacing an existing op.
Removing a convolution on edge 0->3 deleted useful capacity and hurt across datasets (exps 64,67,70).
Filling an empty node2->output edge with a 3x3 conv adds a new computational path and was positive on all datasets (exps 74,80).
When edge 1->3 is absent, removing edge 0->1 kills node 1's main contribution and caused large drops (exps 94,97).
Replacing a 3x3 conv on edge 1->2 with identity removes depth on the longest path and hurt strongly (exps 52,54,58).
Adding a conv on a previously empty input->node1 edge activates the deep path and gave gains (exps 24,30).
Removing a 3x3 conv on node2->output was often neutral-to-positive given redundant conv paths (exps 2,5,7), whereas removing 1x1/skip/pool there hurt more (exps 3,6,9,10).

raw:
Each hypothesis below rests on a few edits where only the parent changes. The evidence is thin, typically 2–5 experiments per condition. I weighted conditions where the measured deltas lined up in sign across all three datasets, and used known NAS-Bench-201 structure to break ties.

- **Edge 4 → avg_pool_3x3:** every parent with e4=nor_conv_3x3 lost accuracy on all datasets (experiments 41–43, 48). Swapping out a strong conv costs more than swapping out a weak op.
- **Edge 4 → none:** removing a skip on e4 helped a lot (84, 89). Removing a 3x3 conv usually hurt (81, 83, 90). With e3=skip_connect, every case was negative (81, 83, 88).
- **Edge 3 → skip_connect:** this helps most when it adds a residual where e3 was none (15, 17).
- **Edge 3 → none:** removing a convolution on e3 hurt (63, 64, 67, 70).
- **Edge 5 → nor_conv_3x3:** this helps when it fills an empty e5 (74, 80).
- **Edge 0 → none:** this was very harmful when e4=none (94, 97). In that case node 1's main contribution is cut off.
- **Weakest support:**
  - Edge 2 → skip_connect with e2=nor_conv_3x3: 52, 54 and 58 hurt on every dataset, but 51 and 60 were mixed.
  - Edge 0 → nor_conv_3x3 with e0=none: two supporting cases, one of them close to zero.
  - Edge 5 → none with e5=nor_conv_3x3: three of five cases point the right way, and 1 and 8 cut against it.
